title: docs(plugin-view): ObjectView.dataSource has no context fallback — delete the promise, pin the behaviour
body:
Fixes #7842

⚠️ Angle-bracket shapes are spelled out in words throughout this body (JSX elements, generic parameters). GitHub's body sanitizer eats tag-shaped fragments on save, and backticks and fenced blocks do not protect them — a paragraph written to show a type would render as if it showed nothing.

## The measurement, which is the whole card

`ObjectViewProps.dataSource` carried this one line above its own declaration:

> If not provided, falls back to `SchemaRendererProvider` context.

on a prop declared `dataSource: DataSource` — required, no question mark. One of the two had been wrong for the prop's entire life. **The type is right; the prose was stale.**

`packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` holds no context read at all:

- No `useContext`, and no `SchemaRendererContext` import. Before this change, the only occurrence of the string `SchemaRendererProvider` anywhere in the file was the sentence itself.
- Not `useElementDataSource` either — the hook `@object-ui/react` publishes for exactly this fallback, and which `plugin-form` and `ElementDataSourceGate` really do use. `packages/plugin-view/src/` has zero references to it.
- The value travels from this prop into `useSettledSchema(schemaKey, dataSource)` at `:653`, and that shared hook has no context read either: given no source it settles with `ready: true, def: null`.

Every consumption site **guards** on the prop instead of resolving one — `:668` `if (!dataSource?.onMutation …) return;`, `:786` `if (!dataSource || !schema.objectName) return;`, and the single `dataSource.find()` call sits behind that second guard.

There is no export-versus-internal split to report: `index.tsx` re-exports `./ObjectView` directly (`:12`, `:18`), so the published symbol and the component that renders are the same one.

## What the component actually does when `dataSource` is absent

tsc refuses the omission at the call site, so this state is only reachable from an untyped JS host, or through the registered renderer described below. When it is reached: **nothing throws and nothing is fetched.** `useSettledSchema` settles with a null definition; the mutation-subscription effect and the non-grid fetch effect both return early; the value is forwarded verbatim to ObjectGrid / SchemaRenderer, and ObjectGrid's own `dataSource` is declared OPTIONAL (`packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx:411`). The view renders its chrome and stays empty.

That is a description of behaviour, not of the comment: the prop guards by doing nothing, which is what makes "required" the honest declaration.

## The sentence was misfiled, not invented

It describes something real in this package, one file over. `ObjectViewRenderer` (`packages/plugin-view/src/index.tsx:58-64`) — the renderer registered for the `object-view` tag and its `view` alias — is what does it: it calls `useContext` on `SchemaRendererContext`, takes `ctx?.dataSource ?? null`, and hands the result to this prop.

So a **schema-driven** host mounted under a provider does get the provider's adapter; a host writing an ObjectView element in TSX does not. That distinction is why the pin below holds both halves. A reader told only "there is no fallback" would be entitled to re-add the sentence the next time they read the registered renderer.

## Scope: no accept set moves here

Comment text and a new test. The declaration is untouched, so the published accept set of `@object-ui/plugin-view` is byte-identical.

Branch B of the card — making the prop optional, so the JSDoc becomes true — is deliberately NOT taken here: it widens a published accept set and belongs to a maintainer. It is also not the one-character change it looks like. Measured, by flipping the declaration to optional and re-running the package's type-check:

```
src/ObjectView.tsx(1870,9): error TS2322: Type 'DataSource of ANY or undefined' is not assignable to type 'DataSource of ANY'.
```

`:1870` is the `dataSource` key handed to the host's `renderListView` callback, whose parameter type (`:314`) declares it required. Anyone taking Branch B has to decide what that host callback receives too.

## The pin

`packages/plugin-view/src/__tests__/ObjectView.dataSourceContextFallback-7842.test.tsx`, six tests:

1. **Live control** — an adapter passed AS THE PROP is read on mount. Without it, "the context adapter was never read" would also be true of a harness that cannot observe a read at all.
2. **The pin** — under a real `SchemaRendererProvider` supplying an adapter, an ObjectView with no `dataSource` never touches that adapter.
3. The same render produces chrome rather than an exception.
4. A **type** pin: an object literal omitting `dataSource` under a `ts-expect-error` directive. If the prop ever goes optional the literal compiles, the directive suppresses nothing, and `tsc` fails with TS2578 naming that line.
5. and 6. The other half: the registered `object-view` renderer still resolves `dataSource` from context, and hands down `null` when no provider is mounted.

⭐ This file deliberately does **not** stub `SchemaRendererContext`, unlike every sibling `ObjectView.*.test.tsx` (they replace it with a fresh `createContext(null)`). A future fallback would be written against the real context, directly or through `useElementDataSource`; a provider built on a look-alike context object could not be seen by it, and test 2 would be a false green. Only `SchemaRenderer` is stubbed.

## Verification

Repo root, canonical invocation, on `fef4b95`:

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-view/` — **35 files, 303 tests, all passed** (66.84s). Baseline was 34 files; this PR adds the 35th.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-view/src/__tests__/ObjectView.dataSourceContextFallback-7842.test.tsx --reporter=verbose` — 6/6 named and passed, so the new file provably executed.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-view type-check`, after `turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/plugin-view` (15 tasks, all successful): `tsc --noEmit` exit 0 and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` exit 0. `--listFiles` confirms the new test file is one of the 47 `plugin-view/src` files in that program — the pin is measured, not merely present.
- `eslint .` in the package: exit 0, **49 files, 0 errors**, 308 pre-existing warnings; the new file contributes 0 of them.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` exit 0 (the empty-frontmatter declaration is the explicit exemption for a comment-and-test change), plus `changeset:check`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit` — all exit 0.

**Ablations, both with an on-disk proof that the mutation landed and a restore verified by hash against the HEAD blob:**

- Implementing the fallback inside ObjectView (import `SchemaRendererContext`, resolve the prop through `useContext`): exactly **one** test turns red — test 2, with its own named message — while the live control and the other four stay green. That is the predicted direction, and it is what makes the negative assertion mean something.
- Flipping the declaration to optional: `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` exits 2 with `TS2578 Unused 'ts-expect-error' directive` at the pin's line, plus the TS2322 quoted above.

Neither ablation needs a `dist` preflight: the vitest alias map resolves every `@object-ui/*` specifier to `src`, and the pin imports `../ObjectView` relatively, so nothing under test is read from a built bundle.

## Out of scope, deliberately

- `packages/app-shell`'s own ObjectView (props typed as ANY) is objectui#7483 — a different component and a different defect. Untouched.
- ⭐ One observation this work measured and pinned but does not fix: `ObjectViewRenderer` hands `null` to a prop declared non-nullable, and nothing complains because the context it reads is typed ANY. That is a downstream instance of objectui#7912 (`SchemaRendererProvider`'s `dataSource` and `SchemaRendererContextType` both typed ANY), which is already open, already carries `needs-user-decision`, and states that narrowing the seam is a public-contract change with its own blast radius. Filed nowhere new on purpose — a second card would be a duplicate of that one. Test 6 pins the `null` as an observation, explicitly not as an endorsement.
